title: Ostbeignet (Cheese Beignets)
description: Prepared with water or milk, grated cheese, and broth.
steps: Boil the butter and water together, add the flour while whisking steadily and let the mixture boil until it releases from the pan, then pour it out and press out the whisk well.
When the mixture has cooled, add the grated cheese and work in the eggs one by one.
Stir the mixture for 10 minutes, then form it with two teaspoons dipped in broth into small balls the size of a hazelnut.
Cook them golden-brown in the broth and place them on gray paper to drain.
The broth should not be too hot, otherwise the balls cannot puff up.
Serve lukewarm, placed on cake paper, to broth.

title: Ostbeignet (Cheese Fritters)
description: Prepared with water or milk, grated cheese, and cream.
steps: Butter and water are brought to a boil, flour is added with steady whisking and the batter is allowed to boil until it releases from the pan, then it is poured out and the whisk is squeezed out well.
When the mass has cooled, the grated cheese is added and the eggs are worked in one at a time.
The mass is stirred for 10 minutes, then formed with two teaspoons, which are dipped in cream, into small balls the size of a hazelnut.
These are cooked golden brown in the cream and laid out on greaseproof paper to drain.
The cream should not be too hot, otherwise the balls cannot swell.
Served lukewarm, arranged on pastry paper, with consommé or bouillon.

title: Ostkrutong (Cheese Croutons)
description: Prepared with bread, egg white, and grated cheese.
steps: Cut out the bread slices with a drinking glass into round cakes (wipe and brush the edges).
Spread butter on one side.
Whisk the egg white a few times with a fork and add the grated cheese.
Mix the cheese mixture well and spread it on the buttered bread rounds.
Place them on a buttered baking sheet.
Just before serving, toast them quickly in a hot oven.
Serve warm with broth, clear soups or purées.
The egg white can be omitted and the butter merely mixed with the cheese before spreading on the bread.

title: Ostkäx (Cheese Crackers)
description: Prepared with cheese, grated cheese, and butter.
steps: The butter is washed (the water is worked out well) and stirred until it becomes white and fluffy.
The egg yolk and sugar are stirred for 10 minutes, then the butter and flour are added and the dough is worked until it becomes smooth.
It is allowed to stand in a cold room for 2 hours, then rolled out to an oblong cake of 2 mm. thickness, which is pricked closely.
It is cut out into slanted squares, which are placed on a well-cleaned baking sheet and baked a beautiful golden color in regular oven heat.
For the cheese filling, the butter is stirred with the cheese until it becomes white and fluffy.
The cheese filling is spread on half of the crackers and the other crackers are placed on top with the pricked side up.
Served with consommé or bouillon.

title: Ostronsås (Oyster Sauce)
description: A sauce made with oysters, broth, and egg yolks.
steps: Open the oysters, the beard and the water from the oysters are poured into a pan together with the broth, which is allowed to boil for 10–15 minutes; strain and should yield 5 dcl.
Blanch the oysters in lightly salted water for 2–3 minutes
Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, dilute with the broth and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes
Add the egg yolks whipped with cream and let the sauce simmer
Add the blanched and cleaned oysters and season with the seasonings, sherry and lemon juice and serve with fish dishes, chicken or veal

title: Ostsufflé (Cheese Soufflé)
description: Prepared with grated cheese, white pepper, and breadcrumbs.

ingredients.name: butter (10 g) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 0.5 tbsp butter (10 g) for the mold

steps: Fry butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the milk and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes. Pour it into a bowl; when it has cooled, add the egg yolks one at a time and stir the mixture for 10 minutes. Mix in the grated cheese together with the seasonings and the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks. Taste the mixture, pour it into a buttered and breadcrumb-strewn pie form and bake in ordinary oven heat for about 45 minutes.

title: Oxjärpar (Beef Birds with Filling)

Spread the filling on the meat slices, which are rolled up with the filling inside, then treated and fried as in the previous recipe.

Whip up the sauce and pour over the rolls; can, if desired, be seasoned with tomato puree.
Serve with pressed potatoes.

title: Oxjärpar (Beef Cutlets Shaped Like Game Bird Breasts)
description: Prepared with beef, fat, and white pepper.

title: Oxrulader (Beef Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with beef, lard, and white pepper.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water and cut it into thin slices, which are beaten well.
On each of them is placed a thin, well-seasoned lard slice, and the rolls are rolled up and bound tightly in two places.
They are browned in the butter, and flour is sprinkled over.
The rolls are thereafter diluted with the boiling liquid and are allowed to slowly roast with a tightly closed lid, until they feel tender when tested with a whisk.
The strings are removed, the rolls are laid up high on carrot, and the sauce is poured over.

title: Oxrulader (Swedish Beef Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with lard, white pepper, and broth or water.
steps: The meat, which should have hung until tender, is dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water, cut into 12 slices, which are well beaten and covered with the lard slices.
These are sprinkled with a mixture of salt and pepper and the meat slices are rolled up tightly and bound in two places with fine twine, dipped in boiling water, or fastened together with toothpicks.

The rolls are well browned in the butter and sprinkled with flour; the boiling broth or water, mixed with a little meat extract or soy sauce, is poured on, after which they are allowed to simmer slowly with a tight lid, 2 1/2–3 hours.
During this time the pot is shaken often so that the rolls do not burn.
They are placed on a warm platter, the strings are cut away and the sauce is whisked well, thinned if necessary, tasted and poured over the rolls.
Served with boiled or pressed potatoes.

title: Oxsvanssoppa (Oxtail Soup)
description: A soup made with oxtail, beef, and onions.
steps: Rinse the oxtail in cold water, scald in boiling water, dry with a cloth and chop into pieces at the joints.
Split the largest pieces crosswise.
Rinse the meat quickly, dry it and cut into smaller pieces.
Peel the onion, prepare the roots and cut them into pieces, rinse the parsley and bind it together with the bay leaf.
Brown the butter in an iron pot, add the meat and vegetables and let them brown over gentle heat for about 1 hour.
Then add 1/4 liter of the boiling stock, which under even stirring is reduced to gelatin.

When the gelatin has taken on a nice dark brown color without burning, add the rest of the stock and let the soup cook slowly with a tightly closed lid for about 3 hours or until the meat is completely tender.
Remove it with a slotted spoon, trim the tail pieces, cut the meat into small pieces and place in the soup bowl.
Strain the soup, skim well, bring to a boil, bind with the cornstarch flour mixed in 1/2 cup cold water, and let it boil under stirring for 5 minutes.
Season with the spices, wine and tomato puree and pour over the meat in the soup bowl.
Serve very hot. If desired, a cooked carrot can be cut into nice figures and served as a garnish in the soup.

title: Oäkta Savarin (False Savarin)
description: Prepared with melted butter, wheat flour, and buttermilk.

ingredients.name: For the mold: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: For the mold: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.)

steps: The eggs and sugar are stirred vigorously for 20 minutes, thereafter the melted but cooled butter is added, the wheat flour, which should be well sifted with the baking powder, and the buttermilk.

The batter is stirred well, is poured immediately into a buttered and breadcrumb-strewn ring mold and is baked in ordinary oven temperature for approximately 1/2 hour, or until the cake, when tested with a whisk, feels dry.
A clear, thin syrup is boiled from the sugar and water, to which wine or arrack is added.
The cake is turned out, the mold is filled halfway with sugar syrup, after which the cake is immediately placed in and is allowed to stand until it has absorbed all the syrup.
The savarin is turned out of the mold and placed on a flat glass plate with cake paper.
Garnish and serve as in the previous recipe.

title: Paltbröd (Blood Bread)
description: A bread preparation made with blood, beer, and rye flour.
steps: Strain the blood and whisk well together with the beer
Add the flour, salt and dissolved yeast, work the dough well and let it rise
When it has risen to double its size, add the lard, spices and syrup, and let the dough rise once more
Form into oblong loaves or round cakes (in the latter case, make indentations with a knife)
Let rise again and bake in good oven heat
When the oblong loaves have cooled, slice them and dry well in the oven
Hang the cakes on sticks from the ceiling to dry

title: Panerade Rotsellerier (Breaded Celery Root)
description: Prepared with celeriac, rusks, and water.
steps: Wash, brush, and peel the celeriac roots. Place in cold water with salt and cook until soft, tested with a whisk.

Alternative: if desired, the celeriac roots can be cooked unpeeled, which gives them a stronger celery flavor.

steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water, cut it into cubes and pass it 2-3 times through a meat grinder.

From the ground meat, thin round steaks are formed, which are sprinkled with pepper and salt. They are chopped lightly with a knife, and the edges are evened well, so that they retain their shape during frying.

title: Pannkakspudding med hachi (Pancake Pudding with Hachi)
description: A pudding made with broth, white pepper, and meat.

ingredients.name: cooked or fried minced meat for hachi
ingredients.sourceText: 4 cups cooked or fried minced meat for hachi

ingredients.name: unskimmed milk for pancake batter
ingredients.sourceText: 6 cups unskimmed milk for pancake batter

steps: Melt butter and flour together, thin with broth, and let the sauce cook for a few minutes. Add the meat, bring the stew to a boil and season. Lastly stir in the egg yolk.
Prepare the pancake batter in the usual way, and make thin pancakes fried on only one side. Place them with the unfried side up on a deep plate or in a fireproof mold.
Spread a moderately thick layer of hachi on each pancake; place the next pancake on top with the fried side up. Continue until the mold is full.
Pour the egg custard over the pancakes, and place the pudding in the oven to set and turn a beautiful light golden color.
If desired, the egg custard can be omitted. Serve the pudding with meat gravy or clarified butter.

title: Pannkaksrisoller (Pancake Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with meat, breadcrumbs, and eggs.

ingredients.name: For the thin pancakes: 3 eggs, 600 ml milk, 90-100 g flour, 1 tsp salt (5 g)

ingredients.name: For the pan: 2 tbsp butter (40 g)
ingredients.sourceText: For the pan: 2 tbsp butter (40 g)

ingredients.name: For the stew: 300 g boneless roasted meat, 1 tin of mushrooms (250 ml), 2 tbsp butter (40 g), 4 tbsp flour (40 g), 400 ml stock, 1 egg yolk, 100 ml thick cream, salt, white pepper

ingredients.name: For frying: 200 ml finely crushed breadcrumbs, 3 tbsp butter (60 g)
ingredients.sourceText: For frying: 200 ml finely crushed breadcrumbs, 3 tbsp butter (60 g)

steps: For the pancake batter, whisk the ingredients well with a wire whisk, then let the batter rest for 1 hour to rise.
Cut the meat into fine cubes.

Cut the mushrooms likewise into cubes and fry in butter until clear, then press them up with a spoon; fry the flour with the butter for 2 minutes, add the stock and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolk with the cream and add to the sauce, then let it simmer.
Add the meat and mushrooms and season the stew with spices.
Heat a pancake pan slowly, melt the butter in a water bath and brush the pan with it.
Make thin pancakes from the batter, browning them on one side only.
Arrange them on a cutting board and distribute the meat mixture on them, roll them up and fry in breadcrumbs and butter until golden.

title: Pannkaksrisoller (Pancake Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with meat, mushrooms, and broth.

ingredients.name: For the pan: 2 msk. butter (40 gr.)

ingredients.name: For the stew: 3 hg. boneless, fried meat

ingredients.name: For frying: 2 dcl. finely crushed rusks

steps: For the pancake batter, whisk the ingredients well with a steel whisk, then let the batter rest for 1 hour to swell.
Cut the meat into fine cubes.
Cut the mushrooms likewise into cubes and fry them in butter until clear, then press them out with a spoon.
Fry the flour with the butter for 2 minutes, add the broth and let the sauce simmer for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolk with the cream and add it to the sauce, then let it simmer.
Add the meat and mushroom and season the stew with spices.
Heat a pancake pan slowly, melt the butter in a water bath and brush the pan with it.
Make thin pancakes from the batter, browning them on one side only.
Lay them on a cutting board, sprinkled with finely crushed rusks, with the fried side up.
Cut the pancakes in half, place 1 msk. of the stew on each half and fold the pancake well so it takes the form of an oblong croquette.
Carefully turn the rolls in crushed rusks and fry them a nice brown in butter.
Place them on a hot platter, garnish with parsley and serve with brown mushroom sauce or clarified butter.
Pancakes can be filled and fried in the same way and served for the smorgasbord.

title: Pastej med fågelstuvning (Pastry with Poultry Stew)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolk, grouse, and meat.

ingredients.name: Remains of grouse or other poultry (3-4 hg.)
ingredients.sourceText: Remains of grouse or other poultry (3-4 hg.)

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the form
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 gr.) for the form

steps: Prepare the shortcrust dough as in recipe no. 35 and let it rest 1 hour.

Cut the poultry remains into slices. Break the carcass and set it to boil in 1 liter of water, added with the meat extract, salt and 1 bouquet (1 leek, 3 parsley stems, 1 celery top). Let the stock boil approximately 2 hours, or until it has a good flavor, then strain and skim it.
Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the stock and let the sauce boil for 5 minutes. Season it with the tomato puree and spices, finish with the beaten egg yolk and finally stir in the wine.
Roll out the dough to approximately 1/2 cm. thickness and with it line a well-buttered, smooth pastry form. The dough should hang 2 cm. over the edge of the form.
Place the poultry slices in and pour in enough sauce so that it nearly covers the meat. (The remaining sauce is thinned with more stock and served with the pastry.)
Fold over the edge that hangs over the form over the stew and place a lid of dough on top. Garnish with figures of dough and brush with beaten egg.
Bake the pastry in a warm oven for approximately 1 hour. Place the form on a plate with tart paper and wrap it with a broken napkin.
Serve as a middle course.

sourceSteps: Prepare the shortcrust dough as in no. 35 and let it rest 1 hour.

Cut the poultry remains into slices. Break up the carcass and set it to boil in 1 liter of water, added with the meat extract, salt and 1 bouquet (1 leek, 3 parsley stalks, 1 celery top). Let the broth boil for about 2 hours, or until it has good flavor, then strain and skim it.
Fry butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the broth and let the sauce boil 5 minutes. Season it with the tomato puree and spices, bind with the whisked egg yolk and finally stir in the wine.
Roll out the dough to about 1/2 cm thickness and line a well-buttered, smooth pie form with it. The dough should hang 2 cm over the edge of the form.

Bake the pie in a warm oven for about 1 hour. Place the form on a dish with baking paper and wrap with a broken napkin.
Serve as a course between courses.

title: Pastej med Harfärs (Hare Meat Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with hare, cream, and egg yolks.
steps: Prepare the pastry dough as in no. 34.

Skin the hare and remove the organs; cut away the head, paws and flanks, then rinse the hare well and dry it. Remove all membranes and cut the hare into pieces. Cut the meat from the bones and scrape it. Pass it 8 times through a meat grinder, the last 3 times together with the butter.

Place the forcemeat in a bowl and stir for about 1 hour, gradually adding the cream by the tablespoon. Pass the forcemeat through a fine sieve, then stir in the egg yolks, egg white and the truffle cut into strips, as well as a little of the truffle juice.
Season the forcemeat with the spices and cook a small test portion in salted water. If the forcemeat is too firm, add a little more cream; if too soft, add a beaten egg.

Roll out the pastry dough to about 1/2 cm. thickness and line a tart form with removable ring. The dough should hang 2 cm. over the edge of the form. Place the forcemeat inside, fold the dough over and brush the edge with egg white. Place a lid of dough over the forcemeat. Brush the lid with egg white and garnish with the remaining dough cut into beautiful figures. Around the edge place a strip of dough, neatly crimped.
Bake the pie in good oven heat for about 1 1/2 hours. After 10 minutes remove the tart ring. Serve the pie as a side dish, warm or cold, with a sharp sauce made from the hare bones.

title: Pastej på stekt kött och ris (Meat and Rice Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with rice, meat, and cream.

ingredients.name: 1/2 weight butter to the dough (about 165 gr.)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 weight butter to the dough (about 165 gr.)

ingredients.name: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 msk. butter (10 gr.) for the mold

ingredients.name: 1 medium-sized salted cucumber or 12 pickled onions
ingredients.sourceText: 1 medium-sized salted cucumber or 12 pickled onions

ingredients.name: 3 dcl. roasting sauce or 2 dcl. broth
ingredients.sourceText: 3 dcl. roasting sauce or 2 dcl. broth

steps: Whip the cream to stiff peaks and work in enough flour to make a reasonably firm dough.
Weigh the dough and incorporate half the weight of butter to the dough as for regular butter dough.
When the dough has rested, roll it out to a cake about 1 cm. thick and line a fluted or smooth baking pan (buttered with the butter) holding about 2 lit.; cut out a lid for the pan.
Cover the butter dough with thin butter paper and fill the pan with peas, place in a warm oven and bake until half done.
Pour out the peas and remove the paper.
Rinse the rice, scald it in hot water, add it to the boiling milk and let it cook until tender, then pour out and let it cool, stirring often.
Mix with the egg yolks and salt; last, fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Cut the meat into thin, even slices or into fine dice.
Chop the cucumber or onion finely.
Layer the meat and rice in the pan alternately, sprinkling a little of the chopped cucumber or onion and spices on each layer of meat, and pour a little sauce or broth.
Place the butter dough lid on top, press down around the edges and bake the pudding in a warm oven for about 3/4 hour, or until the dough is completely tender, which is tested with a whisk.
Turn the pudding out onto a round platter, garnish around with small squares of butter dough and serve with brown gravy sauce if desired.

title: Pastejer I (Pastries I)
description: A pastry dish made with egg yolk, cream, and sweet almonds.
steps: Prepare the butter dough as in recipe no. 33.
Roll out the dough to approximately 3 mm thickness and cut with a round measure into cakes, with which small, smooth pastry forms are lined.
For the filling, blend the eggs, cream, flour, sugar and the blanched and ground almond in a saucepan and whisk over the fire until the cream simmers and is thick.
Lift it off and stir until it becomes cold.
Fill the pastries to 3/4 with cream, place on a baking sheet and bake in a warm oven without a bottom sheet.
When they are half-baked, brush the dough edges with egg yolk to get a nice color.
When the pastries are well baked, turn them out carefully, flip them, place on cake paper and serve warm with consommé or clear broth.
The pastries can also be filled with chicken forcemeat (see quenelles of chicken forcemeat) and baked in the same way.

Fill them to 3/4 with cream; place a lid of dough over and press firmly against the edge.
Cut the rest of the dough into narrow strips, which are laid in squares over the lid.
Bake and serve as in the previous recipe.
When they are half-baked, brush them with the whisked egg to get a nice color.

title: Patentbiff (Patent Beef Steak)
description: Prepared with beef, smoked ham, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: 6 hg. beef top round or boneless inner thigh
ingredients.sourceText: 6 hg. beef top round or boneless inner thigh

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the eggs
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 gr.) for the eggs

steps: The meat is dried with a cloth wrung out in hot water, and cut across the muscle fibers into approximately 1 cm. thick slices, which are beaten on both sides, peppered and salted.
Thin slices are cut from the smoked ham.
A frying pan is heated slowly, the butter is browned in it, the steaks are laid in and fried approximately 1 minute on each side, after which they are placed on a warm serving platter.
The pan is whisked out with the boiling broth and the sauce is poured over the steaks.
The pan is heated again and the ham slices are placed, one slice is laid on each steak.
Meanwhile the eggs are fried in a griddle and one egg is placed on each steak.
They are served with freshly boiled or fried potatoes as a breakfast dish.

title: Persiljefylld Kalvbringa (Parsley-Filled Veal Breast)
description: Prepared with veal, parsley, and white pepper.
steps: Use the front part of the breast or the so-called breast and do not break the bones.
Bone the breast carefully and cook broth on the bones to dilute the roast with.
Prepare the meat and rub with the seasonings.
Rinse the parsley, wrap in a cloth, clean and chop coarsely and work into the butter.

Spread the parsley butter on the inside of the breast, then roll it up and sew it securely, then brown it in butter, sprinkle with the remaining seasonings, and let it roast in a pot or oven for about 3 hours.
During roasting baste the meat every 10 minutes and dilute with the boiling broth.
When the roast is tender, remove all threads, then cut into even slices, which are laid together so that the roast looks whole.
Place on a warm platter, garnish with salad or parsley, serve with vegetables or boiled potatoes, salads and strained sauce with cream added (see recipe 429).
If desired, the meat can be diluted with some cream and some broth.

title: Persiljespäckad fårstek (Parsley-Larded Lamb Roast)
description: Prepared with lamb, parsley, and broth or water.
steps: Crack the bones and wash the lamb roast with a cloth dipped in hot water.
Mix the parsley well with 1 tbsp of the butter, make holes in the roast with a pointed wooden stick, and insert some of the parsley butter in each hole.
Place the roast in a long pan, buttered with cold butter, and put in the oven to brown.
When well browned, salt it, add the allspice berries, and add the boiling liquid.
The roasting takes 1½-2 hours. During this time, baste the roast around every ten minutes.
Strain the meat drippings, skim, and prepare the sauce according to general rules for sauces.

title: Persiljespäckad lammstek (Parsley-Larded Roast Lamb)
description: Prepared with lamb, parsley, and white pepper.
steps: The roast is treated as in no. 531 and the shank is cut off.
The parsley is cleaned, rinsed, wrung in a cloth, chopped coarsely and worked into the butter, which is then allowed to harden in a cold place.

title: Petits-choux (20 pieces)
description: Prepared with wheat flour, water, and butter.
steps: Bring water, butter, and sugar to a boil, whisk in the flour, and let the batter cook until it leaves the sides of the pan.
When most of the heat has passed, stir in the egg yolks one at a time.

On well-cleaned and buttered baking sheets, place large spoonfuls of the batter.
Bake in good oven heat, taking care not to open the oven door before 10 minutes have passed.
When the pastries have cooled, cut a lid in each, and fill them with cream or whipped cream.

title: Petits-choux (Choux Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with butter, milk, and sugar.
steps: Melt the butter in a saucepan with a round bottom, pour in the milk and bring to a boil with sugar and lemon zest.
Whisk in the flour while at a rolling boil and let the mixture cook until it leaves the pan.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly, then stir in the eggs one at a time and beat the mixture for 10 minutes.

The mixture can either be piped through a fluted pastry bag onto a well-buttered baking sheet into oblong pastries (éclairs), which are split after baking and filled with some cream, or placed by spoon into round buns (choux); these are filled with whipped cream flavored with vanilla.
Bake immediately in a not-too-hot oven, taking care not to open the oven door before 8-10 minutes have passed.

title: Petits-choux Pudding (Cream Puff Pudding)
description: A pudding made with cream, juice, and butter.

ingredients.name: boiling water for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 tablespoons boiling water for the mold

steps: Place the sugar in a buttered, slightly warm frying pan and brown lightly, then add the boiling water, and use this mixture to coat a fireproof mold.
Fry the butter and flour for 2 minutes, add the cream, and let the mixture boil for 5 minutes, then pour it out and let it cool.
Stir in the egg yolks one at a time together with the sugar, the finely grated lemon zest and lemon juice, and stir the mixture for 10 minutes.
Finally, fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the mixture into the coated mold and bake in a water bath in the oven for about 1 hour.
Serve the pudding immediately when it is ready with vanilla, lemon, or fruit sauce. If desired, the pudding can be turned out.

description: Prepared with cucumbers, tomatoes, and green beans.
steps: Sprinkle the cucumbers and tomatoes with 1 tbsp. salt and let them stand for one day.
Clean and rinse the vegetables; cut the peas, beans, cauliflower and carrots into nice pieces.
Blanch all the vegetables (except cucumbers and tomatoes) separately in lightly salted water (1 liter water, 1 tbsp. salt), rinse with cold water and let drain on cloth.
Dry the cucumbers and tomatoes on cloth and cover with quadruple linen.
When the cucumbers are cold, bind the jar well.
Store in the cellar.
Ready after 5-6 weeks.

title: Pilau på lam (Lamb Pilau)
description: Prepared with lamb, onion, and carrots.
steps: Wash the breast with a cloth dipped in hot water and cut into nice pieces.
Place to boil in warm water, skim, salt, and cook for 1 hour, then remove and strain the broth.
Peel and coarsely chop the onion and brown in half the butter, add the meat and brown likewise.
Add one liter of the strained broth and let the meat cook slowly until tender.
Clean the vegetables, cut into fine strips and brown in the other half of the butter, then add broth and let the vegetables cook—preferably each separately—until soft.
Rinse the rice and place in 2 liters boiling salted water and cook until soft, stirring occasionally with a fork.
Strain the rice and place in the warming oven to dry.
Place the meat in the middle of the serving platter, and the rice and vegetables in groups around it. Garnish the dish with parsley.
Strain the sauce, skim, and thicken if desired.

Peel and finely chop the onion and brown it in half the butter, add the meat and brown it likewise. Add one liter of the strained broth, and let the meat simmer slowly until tender. Prepare the root vegetables, cut into fine strips and brown in the other half of the butter, then add broth and let the vegetables simmer—preferably separately—until soft.

Rinse the rice and place in 2 liters boiling salted water and simmer until soft, stirring occasionally with a fork. Drain and place in a warm oven to dry. Arrange the meat in the center of the serving plate, and rice and vegetables in groups around it. Garnish with parsley.
Strain the sauce, skim, and thicken if desired.

title: Pirog med köttstuvning (Meat Pie)
description: A pastry dish made with meat, wheat flour, and brandy.

ingredients.name: cooked meat cut into cubes
ingredients.sourceText: 3 cups cooked meat cut into cubes

steps: Prepare the butter dough as fine butter dough; roll out half of the dough to a bottom (suitable to the serving dish). Lay this on a baking sheet and bake light brown.
For the stewing, fry butter and flour together, dilute the bouillon into it, and let the sauce simmer 10 minutes.
Place the meat and peas into the sauce, and season the stewing with salt and white pepper.
Spread the stewing on the baked butter dough bottom. Roll out the rest of the dough to a lid, lay it over the stewing and press down at the edges.
Garnish the lid with squares or leaves of butter dough. Brush with egg, and bake the pirog thereafter about 10-15 minutes in good oven heat. Serve at once.

title: Pirog på Lax (Salmon Pirog)
description: Prepared with salmon, rice, and cream.
steps: Rinse the rice groats and blanch in hot water, then place in boiling salted water, thin with the thick cream and allow to cook until soft, then pour out and let cool.
Rinse the salmon, cut into slices and let soak in 1 lit. skimmed milk for approximately 3 hours, take out, wrap in a cloth or white paper and cut into cubes.
Fry the onion in the butter. Chop the eggs finely.
Prepare the pastry dough as in no. 33 and roll out to a 1 1/4 cm. thick cake.
From an ovenproof dish on which the pirog shall be baked, take a measure. This is done most easily by cutting a pattern of paper and thereafter cutting out the dough with a pastry wheel.
Place the dough base on the dish and a 3 cm. wide strip of dough is placed in a ring on top of the base and fastened with egg white.
Mix the rice groats with the salmon, onion and eggs and place inside the ring.
Cover the pirog with a pastry dough lid of the same size as the base, and fasten the lid to it with egg white.
Garnish the lid in squares with narrow pastry dough strips and in each square make a small cut with a fork so that the dough rises and the dish gets a neat appearance.
Brush the pirog with egg white, which must not drip down the sides, because it prevents the pastry dough from rising.
Bake in a warm oven.

title: Pistacieglace (Pistachio Frozen Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, pistachio, and sweet almonds.
steps: The sweet almonds and bitter almonds are blanched, passed through an almond grinder or grated and boiled with the thin cream for approximately 10 minutes, after which the mixture is strained.
The cream is brought to a boil again and blended with vigorous whisking into the egg yolks.
The mixture is then allowed to simmer over the heat until it thickens, after which it is lifted from the heat.
It is flavored with sugar and arrack, colored and put into an ice cream machine to freeze.
When the frozen mixture is half frozen, the blanched and chopped pistachio almonds and the cream whipped to peaks are folded in, after which freezing is continued.
Pistachio frozen cream is served in glasses together with some white frozen cream.

title: Plommonkompott (Plum Compote)
description: A plum compote made with sugar and water.

ingredients.name: 1 1/2 lit. gula, röda ell. gröna plommon

steps: Make a clear, syrupy syrup from the sugar and water and let it cool.
Peel the plums, halve them, remove the pits, place them directly in the sugar syrup, sprinkle with powdered sugar and let stand 2-3 hours.
Crush half of the pits; blanch the kernels in boiling water and peel them.
Remove the plums with a slotted spoon and cook the syrup until it is syrupy, then add the plums and kernels and cook for 2-3 minutes.
Pour the compote into a warm compote bowl and serve cold with whipped cream.

title: Plommonspäckad svinkarré (Prune-Larded Pork Loin)
description: Prepared with lemons, prunes, and broth or water.
steps: Wash the loin with a cloth dipped in hot water and rub it with the lemon until all its juice is extracted.
Rinse the prunes and parboil them (the water is used for basting during roasting), remove the pits and cut them into four parts; lard the loin with these in dense rows.
Place it in good oven heat to brown in the butter, salt it and add the cooled prune water, then let it cook slowly about 1 hour.
Add the hot broth during roasting, and baste the loin every ten minutes.
Serve with its own sauce, which is strained and carefully skimmed.
If the sauce is to be thickened, prepare it according to general rules for sauces, and a little cream can be added in that case.

description: A sauce made with prunes, water, and sugar.
steps: The plums are rinsed and are then allowed to soak for 2-3 hours in the water in which they are to be cooked.

The sauce is boiled up, tasted for seasoning and served.

title: Plommonsås (Plum Sauce)
description: A sauce made with prune, potato starch, and water.
steps: Rinse the plums in several changes of lukewarm water and wrap them in a cloth.
Crush half of them in a stone mortar so that the pits are broken.
Let the crushed and whole plums soak for several hours in the water in which they will be cooked.
Cook until completely soft, then press through a hair sieve.
Cook the fruit purée with the sugar and thicken as in no. 460.
Taste and season with a little lemon juice if desired.
Serve warm or cold. Sauce of dried cherries is prepared in the same way.

title: Plumpudding (Plum Pudding for 6 persons)
description: A pudding made with apples, currants, and raisins.
steps: Peel the apples, core them and chop finely.
Clean and wash the currants, rinse the raisins, remove the seeds and chop them, cut the candied fruit into thin slices.
Free the beef suet from membranes and chop finely together with the wheat flour.
Mix all dry ingredients well together.
Add the egg yolks, brandy and water gradually, working the mixture vigorously for 2½ to 3¾ hours.
Pack the mixture together, place a plate on top, and let it rest at least two days.
When the pudding is to be cooked, beat the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold carefully into the mixture.
Pour the batter into a buttered mold, cover with buttered paper and cook in a water bath for at least 3 hours.
Serve with flaming sauce.

title: Plumpudding (Plum Pudding)
description: A pudding made with apples, raisins, and sultana.

ingredients.name: 1 msk. butter (20 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 1 msk. butter (20 gr.) for the mold

ingredients.name: 2 msk. wheat flour (20 gr.) for the mold
ingredients.sourceText: 2 msk. wheat flour (20 gr.) for the mold

steps: Peel and core the apples and chop finely. Clean, rinse well, split and pit the malaga raisins. Clean and rinse well the sultana raisins and currants. Cut the orange peel into fine dice.
If desired, soak all the fruit in the liqueur two days before the pudding is to be prepared.

Rinse the kidney fat, dry in cloth, clean and chop finely together with the wheat flour. Weigh bread crumbs, soak in milk and squeeze out. Finely grate the zest of orange and lemon, and press out the juice.
Work the kidney fat well with the bread crumbs, then add the fruit and all the other ingredients, and stir the mixture well.
Butter a large fireproof mold and dust with wheat flour, pack the mixture into it, and bind the mold with a buttered and floured napkin, which is tied in a knot on top of the pudding.
Cook the pudding thereafter for about 4 hours in water or steam.
Serve warm or cold with wine sauce or flaming sauce (see no. 457 and 465).

Butter a large ovenproof mold and dust with wheat flour, pack the mixture into it, and bind the mold with a buttered and floured cloth, tying it in a knot on top of the pudding.
Boil the pudding for about 4 hours in water or steam.
Serve warm or cold with wine sauce or flaming sauce (see no. 457 and 465).

title: Plättar (Swedish Pancakes)
description: Prepared with clarified butter, flour, and milk.
steps: Sift the flour into a bowl and mix with salt.
Whip the eggs with two cups of the milk and add to the flour with vigorous whisking.
When the batter is smooth and glossy, stir in half the butter, and when it is well mixed, add the remaining milk.
Let the batter stand for 1 hour so the flour can swell.
Give it a vigorous whip.
Heat the pancake pan slowly, brush with clarified butter, and fry pancakes from the batter.
Thin pancakes can also be fried from the same batter.

title: Polkagrisar (Swedish Striped Candy)
description: Peppermint-flavored candy made with sugar and glucose, with red coloring.
steps: Cook the socker, water, and glykos to hard crack stage, then add 10 drops of peppermint oil.
Pour half of the sugar onto a lightly oiled marble slab and continuously fold the edges inward with an oiled knife until the sugar has cooled.
Pull the sugar between oiled hands or over a hook until it is white, then pull it out into a thin length.

Meanwhile, cook the remaining sugar to caramel stage, color it red with carmine, pour it out, roll it out, and place it on the white sugar which is twisted and cut diagonally into 2—3 cm. long candies.

title: Polsk köttstuvning (Polish Beef Stew)
description: Prepared with beef, rusks, and kidney.
steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water and cut into two large slices, approximately 1 cm thick.
Mix the crushed rusks, kidney fat, parsley, and seasonings with the beaten eggs and work into a smooth paste.
Divide the mixture in half and place on each meat slice.
Roll them up tightly and bind well with string.
Heat the butter in a roasting pan, brown the rolls, and add the boiling broth or water.
Scrub, scrape, and cut the carrots into thick slices. Peel the onions and cut into wedges, then add to the meat.
Let the stew simmer slowly with a tightly fitting lid for approximately 1 1/2 - 2 hours.
Remove the rolls, take off the string, and cut the meat into nice slices. Place on the center of a plate and garnish with the carrots and onion.
Strain and skim the sauce, then pour over the meat.
If desired, peeled potatoes can be added to the stew 1/2 hour before serving is complete, but more liquid must then be used.

title: Polsk äppelkaka (Polish Apple Cake)
description: A cake made with apples, white wine, and sweet almonds.

ingredients.name: butter (10 gr.) for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tbsp. butter (10 gr.) for the pan

steps: Rinse the apples, dry them, peel them, cut them into 6-8 wedges, free them from the cores, place them in a preserving pan together with butter, sugar, wine and water and cook as compote, while shaking the pan often.
Place the apples in a buttered pie form, cook the liquid together until it is syrupy and pour it over them.
Whisk the flour and 1 dcl. of the milk into a slurry.
Whisk the egg yolks and sugar for 15 minutes.
Boil the rest of the milk, add the slurry, let the milk boil again and pour it over the beaten egg yolks with vigorous whisking.
Add the blanched and ground almond, let the cream simmer and whisk it thereafter until it is cold.
Season, if desired, with 1 tbsp. vanilla sugar, then fold in the egg whites beaten to stiff peaks.
Pour the cream over the compote and bake the cake in ordinary oven heat for about 3/4 hour.
Serve warm or cold with whipped cream.

title: Polska Rulader (Polish Beef Rolls)
description: A bread preparation made with beef, onion, and lard.

ingredients.name: 1⅔ kg boneless beef in one cohesive bundle
ingredients.sourceText: 1⅔ kg boneless beef in one cohesive bundle

steps: Wash the meat with a cloth dipped in hot water and cut it into thin slices, which are beaten well, but not so that they break apart.
Peel the onion and chop it finely together with the parsley, and with this sprinkle the meat slices.
Cut the lard into thin slices, which are sprinkled with pepper and salt and placed on top of the meat slices.
On top is placed cleaned and boned anchovy.
Roll the meat slices tightly together and bind them in two places with fine sailcloth twine (previously dipped in hot water) and place them close together in an iron roasting pan brushed with butter.
Thereafter set the rolls on good heat to brown.
Dilute with the boiling water and let them roast 1–1½ hours.
Strain the sauce, skim it and serve as jus.

title: Potatis-petits-choux (Potato Choux Pastries)
description: A pastry dish made with potato, fat, and butter.
steps: Butter and water are brought to a boil, the flour is whisked in under vigorous boiling and the batter is allowed to boil until it releases from the pan and has a golden color.
It is poured out and allowed to cool, whereupon the eggs are worked in one at a time and the batter is stirred for 10 minutes.
The potato mash is prepared as in recipe 677, allowed to cool and added to the batter with vigorous stirring, whereupon the mass is seasoned with spices.

The mass is formed with two spoons, dipped in the fat, into round balls, which, if desired, can be filled with chopped truffle or peas, are fried golden brown in hot fat and placed on blotting paper to drain.
Served as garnish around roasted meat. If the balls are not filled, they should be made very small.

title: Potatisblommor (Potato Flowers)
description: Prepared with potatoes, cream, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: peeled potatoes, approximately 1 1/2 liters unpeeled
ingredients.sourceText: 1 kg peeled potatoes, approximately 1 1/2 liters unpeeled

steps: Rinse the potatoes, brush them, peel thinly, cut into pieces and cook quickly in salted water until soft but not falling apart.
Drain them immediately in a colander and let stand in the front part of the oven for a few minutes to dry, then press through a fine sieve.
Place the puree in a saucepan, add the butter, cream and seasonings and stir the puree with a fork over the heat until it becomes firm.
Remove from the heat and add the egg yolks one at a time while stirring vigorously.
If desired, season the mash with sugar.
Let the puree cool and then press it through a pastry bag with a large star nozzle onto a well-buttered baking sheet in the shape of flowers.
Brush these with beaten egg and bake in a warm oven until they have a beautiful golden yellow color.
Serve as a garnish around roasted meat.

title: Potatiskroketter (Potato Croquettes)
description: Prepared with potatoes, white pepper, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: butter (30 gr) for the dish
ingredients.sourceText: 1 1/2 tbsp butter (30 gr) for the dish

steps: Peel the potatoes thinly, cut into pieces, weigh them and cook quickly in salted water until soft but not falling apart.
Immediately drain in a colander and place in the front of the oven for a few minutes to dry.
Pass the potatoes through a fine sieve.
Place the puree in a saucepan, add the cold butter and seasonings and stir with a fork over the heat until firm.
Remove from heat and add the egg yolks one at a time, stirring constantly with a fork, then taste and adjust seasonings.
Butter a flat dish and spread the mixture thinly so it cools quickly.
Brush the surface with butter so it does not dry out.
Divide the mixture with a spoon into smaller pieces—each piece should weigh about 35 gr—and roll on a floured work surface in the form of corks, pears, buns or round patties.
Dip in the stiffly beaten eggs mixed with cooking oil and seasoned with the spices, then roll in the finely crushed rusks and let sit 1 hour to harden.
Fry golden brown in hot lard and place on absorbent paper to drain.
Serve with roasted meat. If the croquettes are formed as pears, use parsley sprigs or spinach leaves as stems.

ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tablespoon butter for the mold, 2 tablespoons crushed rusks

steps: Peel the potatoes raw, cook and mash them with a fork or press them through a puree press.
Whisk the egg yolks together with the milk and stir into the puree along with the cold butter and seasonings.
Beat the whites to stiff peaks and fold in last.
Place the puree in a buttered and bread-crumb lined mold, sprinkle with crushed rusks and crimp neatly.
Put the pudding in a hot oven to cook through and brown.
It is served with meat dishes in general.

title: Potatissufflé (Potato Soufflé)
description: Prepared with potatoes, cream, and white pepper.

ingredients.name: butter (10 g) for the dish
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 tablespoon butter (10 g) for the dish

steps: Peel the potatoes thinly, cook them and press through a puree press.
Stir the cold butter into the mash with a fork along with the beaten egg yolks and cream.
Add the seasonings and lastly fold in the stiffly beaten egg whites.
Place the mixture in a buttered and bread crumb-lined ovenproof dish and sprinkle with fine bread crumbs.
Bake the soufflé in a good oven heat until it has a beautiful golden brown color, or about 40 minutes.
Serve immediately after removing from the oven as a sandwich course or with roasted meat in general.

title: Potatistårta (Potato Cake)
description: A cake made with potato, sweet almonds, and bitter almonds.

ingredients.name: 15 gr. washed butter for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 15 gr. washed butter for the pan

ingredients.name: crushed rusks for the pan
ingredients.sourceText: 3 tablespoons crushed rusks for the pan

steps: Wash the butter and stir it until it is white and fluffy. Whip the eggs and sugar for 20 minutes and then mix with the butter. Add the potato together with the blanched and ground almonds and fill the batter into a well-buttered and breadcrumb-strewn baking pan and bake in a not too hot oven for about 40 minutes. Take the cake out of the oven and let it stand for 10 minutes before turning it out. When the cake is cold, glaze it with water glaze (see no. 961) and sprinkle, if desired, with 20 gr. finely chopped pistachios. Serve as a dessert with vanilla or lemon sauce.

title: Poularde à la Idun (Chicken à la Idun)
description: Prepared with hen, lemon, and lard.

ingredients.name: clear chicken or veal broth
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter clear chicken or veal broth

ingredients.name: 25 gr. truffle (optional, for larding before stuffing)
ingredients.sourceText: 25 gr. truffle (optional, for larding before stuffing)

steps: Prepare the bird in the usual way, remove the bones and rub the breast and thighs with lemon.
Rinse the rice grains, scald in hot water, add to boiling broth and let cook until half soft, then drain and let cool.
Cut the goose liver and truffle into cubes and mix into the rice with salt, pepper and wine if desired.
Stuff the bird with the rice and sew well closed, then rub with salt, truss and place a lard slice on top, fastening it with fine twine.
Place in a pot just large enough to fit the bird, add the cold broth, cover with lid, place over heat and bring the broth to a simmer, then skim well.
Keep the broth at no more than 90° and let the bird rest at this temperature until tender, about 2 1/2–3 hours.
Test doneness by pricking a larding needle into the thick part of the thigh near the bone; if the liquid that runs out is white, the bird is done.

Cut the bird and arrange on a platter so it appears whole, garnish with the stuffing, salad and parsley and serve with light mushroom sauce prepared from the broth and mixed with thick cream and 40 gr. fine butter.
If desired, lard the bird with 25 gr. truffle before stuffing and trussing.

Rinse the rice grains, scald them in hot water, place them in boiling broth and let them cook until half soft, then drain and let them cool.

Stuff the bird with the rice and sew it well shut, then rub it with salt, place it in position and cover it with the lard slice, which is fastened with fine twine.

Place it in a pot that should be no larger than to accommodate the bird snugly, pour on the cold broth, cover with the lid, place the pot over the fire and heat the broth until it begins to simmer gently, then skim it well.
Do not heat the broth beyond 90 degrees and at this temperature let the chicken lie until it is tender, or about 2 1/2–3 hours.
If you prick with a larding needle in the thick part of the thigh next to the bone and the liquid that seeps out is white, the bird is done.

If desired, the bird can be larded with 25 gr. truffle before it is stuffed and prepared.

title: Poularde, stekt i ugn (Hen Roasted in the Oven)
description: Prepared with capon, lard, and broth.
steps: Prepare the bird in the usual way, salt it inside, truss it, and cover it with the slice of lard, which should be fastened with fine string.
Place it breast up on a rack in a roasting pan so that it does not rest in the fat that collects in the pan.
Place in a warm oven and roast until tender, about 40-50 minutes, basting frequently with melted butter and thinning with broth to reduce the heat.
Cut and garnish as in the previous recipe.
Serve with the strained and skimmed meat gravy or with reduced sauce (see recipe no. 429).

title: Pressgurka (Pressed Cucumber)
description: Prepared with cucumber, vinegar, and white pepper.
steps: Peel the cucumber and cut it into thin slices from the stem downward.
Layer the slices alternately with salt between flat plates, press them, and let them lie for a couple of hours.
Pour off the liquid that forms.
Make a brine from the vinegar, water, sugar, and pepper.
Place the cucumber in it and sprinkle with chopped parsley.

title: Pressylta (Pressed Head Cheese)
description: Prepared with pig's head, meat, and peppercorns.
steps: Split the pig's head, wash and scrape it and then soak it in water for one day.
Change the water a couple of times.
Place the head and calf meat in boiling water so that it covers the meat.
After skimming, add 3 tablespoons of salt and the peppercorns.
Let the meat simmer until it is tender and falls from the bones.
Wring out a towel in hot water and spread it out in a bowl.
Cut the rind into the largest possible pieces and spread it on the towel with skin side down.
Cut the meat and fat into slices while hot.
Next to the rind, place a layer of calf meat sprinkled with pepper and salt, and then a layer of fat, continuing this way with seasonings between each layer.
Place a fat rind on top and tie the towel tightly.
Dip the aspic in the boiling broth and then place it in a press for about 24 hours.
Store it in brine.

title: Pressylta (Pressed Head Cheese)
description: Prepared with pork, veal, and peppercorns.
steps: Split the pig head, wash and scrape it and let it then lie in water for one day. Change the water a couple of times.
Then place the head and veal meat in so much boiling water that it stands over the meat.
After skimming, add 3 msk. of the salt and the peppercorns.
Let the meat cook until it is tender and falls away from the bones.
Wring a towel out in hot water and spread it out in a bowl.
Cut the skin in as large pieces as possible and spread them out on the cloth with skin side down.
Cut the meat and fat into slices while it is hot.
Nearest the skin, place a layer of veal, which is sprinkled with pepper and salt, and then a layer of fat, and so continue alternately with seasonings between each layer.
On top place a fat skin, then tie the towel tightly together.
Dip the sylta in the boiling broth and then place it in a press for about 24 hours.
It is preserved in brine.

title: Pressylta (Pressed Pork Aspic)
description: Prepared with pork, pig's head, and veal.

ingredients.name: white pepper for the aspic
ingredients.sourceText: 3 teaspoons white pepper for the aspic

steps: Split the pig's head, wash it well and soak it overnight in plenty of cold water, changing the water 2 times
Bring the water to a boil, add the head, skin and veal, skim well when it comes to a boil again, then add the salt and other seasonings
Allow the meat to cook until tender and easily comes away from the bones
Remove immediately and take off the skin in pieces as large as possible
Cut the meat and pork into slices or cubes
Dip a kitchen towel in hot water, wring it out and spread it in a dish, place the skin on the towel with the skin side down
Layer with veal, which is sprinkled with pepper and salt, then a layer of pork, and continue alternating layers with seasonings between each layer
Place a large pork skin on top and tie the towel tightly
Heat the aspic for 1/2 hour in the simmering broth and then place it under a press for approximately 12 hours
Store for shorter periods in a towel sprinkled with salt, for longer periods in salt brine
